# Istio CRD compatibility bundle

This directory is the single, cluster-wide Istio CRD bundle installed by Deckhouse.
It intentionally contains one `CustomResourceDefinition` object per YAML file.

## Sources

* The 14 Istio configuration CRDs are copied from the generated bundle in the
  Istio repository at tag `1.29.6` (`manifests/charts/base/files/crd-all.gen.yaml`,
  generated by Istio's Cue OpenAPI generator). Istio 1.29.6 is the source of
  truth for these schemas and storage versions.
* `istiooperators.install.istio.io` is the compatibility CRD historically
  shipped by Deckhouse for Istio 1.25. Upstream Istio no longer included the
  in-cluster operator chart in the 1.25 source tree, so the pinned Deckhouse
  snapshot is used when reconstructing the bundle.
* The five `sailoperator.io` CRDs come from Sail Operator tag `1.25.2`. They are
  required while Istio 1.25 remains supported.

The bundle is a compatibility superset: configuration APIs retain every served
upstream version, including legacy `v1alpha3` and `v1beta1` versions. Kubernetes
is responsible for retaining old `status.storedVersions`; this bundle must not
manually edit that status.

## Updating

From the repository root, run:

```shell
go run ./modules/110-istio/crds/update
```

The updater downloads the Istio and Sail Operator CRDs at the versions listed
above, verifies their pinned SHA-256 checksums, combines them with its embedded
legacy `IstioOperator` CRD, and replaces the bundle only after validation.
Remote sources are pinned rather than read from a moving branch such as `main`.
When changing a source version, update its URL and checksum in the updater and
carefully review the generated diff.

Validate the checked-in bundle without downloading upstream sources with:

```shell
go run ./modules/110-istio/crds/update --check
```

The updater splits multi-document YAML without changing object semantics,
writes one file per CRD, and checks the expected 14 configuration and six
operator CRD names. It also checks that every CRD has exactly one storage
version and that legacy configuration versions remain served. Use
`--output-dir` to operate on a bundle outside the default module directory.
